name: Kuthant
confidence_why: one confirmed first-hand source; 3 other works read were silent
catalog_citation: Black, Paul. 1980. Norman Pama historical phonology. In B. Rigsby and P. Sutton (eds), Papers in Australian Linguistics No. 13: Contributions to Australian Linguistics, 181-239. Pacific Linguistics A-59. Canberra: ANU.
catalog_locator: p.197 (PDF p.17 of), section on Kurtjar/Kuthant phonology; Kurtjar counterpart statement p.196
catalog_quote: Kuthant appears to have a phonology much like that of Kurtjar. ... Kuthant has a vocalic inventory similar to that of Kurtjar, but also possesses a diphthong ia. This diphthong is attested only in interconsonantal position accompanied by length ... Kuthant furthermore has contrastive length in non-initial as well as initial syllables: cf. Kt. tYiku:r, Kr. tYi:kir 'small' ... Stress in Kuthant is non-contrastive and falls on the first long vowel, or on the first vowel if none are long.

audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: every fragment of the deciding quotation is verbatim in the held PL-A59.181 PDF/text at printed pp.196-197 (PDF pp.16-17); locator correct. (2) Deciding source: Black 1980 is a historical-phonology article, but the Kuthant stress sentence is the fieldworker's own first-hand synchronic statement; it explicitly ties stress to vowel length ('first long vowel, or first vowel if none are long') and separately documents contrastive length in non-initial syllables (Kt. tYiku:r vs Kr. tYi:kir), so the 'weight' coding (leftmost CVV, else initial; unbounded; CVV heavy) follows directly from the text.
